name_reason: Follows fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> convention (domain=battle, descriptor=check_battle_end_condition). No address residue. Accurately reflects the function's purpose: computing the default battle win/lose/continue result code.
purpose: Default per-chapter battle-end condition check: writes data_fd2_chapter_event_or_battle_end_code = 2 (victory, all enemies dead), 1 (game over, protagonist dead), or 0 (battle continues).
logic_summary: Initialize result code = 2 (default victory). Loop char index 0..party_member_count-1 over runtime_char array; if a slot is an enemy (bTeam==0 at offset 6) AND alive (CHARFLAG_DEAD bit clear at offset 5), set code = 0 (battle continues, enemies remain). After the loop, if the protagonist (slot 0) has the dead flag set, override code = 1 (game over). Result code is later read by the chapter post-action handler that called this.

returns.semantics: No return value; result is communicated via the global data_fd2_chapter_event_or_battle_end_code (0=continue, 1=game over, 2=victory).

notes: Source comment block (btl_turn.c:307-312) is already concise and accurate (flag=2 victory if all enemies dead, flag=1 game over if protagonist dead, flag=0 continue), matching the decompile exactly -- kept unchanged. Ghidra plate is detailed and consistent with this understanding (algorithm, flag values, 13 chapter callers, interleave layout note) and does not contradict src -- left as-is. Caller count confirmed = 13 via get_function_callers. void function -> params=[]. Struct field offsets in code (pChar[5]=flags, pChar[6]=team) match the Ghidra runtime_char struct (bFlags/bTeam) and are consistent across the codebase (btl_ai.c, btl_aitg.c, chpost.c); the fd2-knowledge strategy-guide layout lists different offsets (0x0D/0x0E) for a different binary/version interpretation, not an issue for this symbol.
